1.explanation:
• BpmnCopyPaste.js handles the paste operation by replaying create commands for each element. It thus emits the same create events as a manual element creation.  
• LabelEditingProvider.js listens for element creation events (create.start / create.end) and unconditionally activates direct editing for tasks and other flow nodes.  
Because paste produces normal create events, the first pasted task gets picked up by LabelEditingProvider and opens its label editor immediately. To fix this, one must adjust either the paste handler (BpmnCopyPaste.js) to flag pasted elements or suppress direct editing in LabelEditingProvider when the source of the create event is a paste.
1.bug_scenario: When you copy and paste a group of elements whose first item is a task, the pasted task immediately opens its name‐editing UI (“direct editing”) even though pasting should not trigger any edit mode. This only happens if the very first pasted element is a task; otherwise no direct editing shows up.

2.explanation:
• BpmnCopyPaste.js – This is where pasted elements are instantiated and (re-)selected. Any workaround to suppress direct editing on paste or to post-process the selection would need to go here.  
• CreateBehavior.js – The generic create behaviour for BPMN shapes triggers direct editing after a shape is created; paste operations internally create shapes and thus fall under this logic. We need to detect ‘paste context’ here and skip the direct editing step.  
• LabelEditingProvider.js – Sets up the direct editing feature and listens for the right events. Changes here can ensure that paste events do not fire into the direct editing lifecycle.  
• LabelEditingPreview.js – Hooks into selection and label clicks to actually open the inline editor. Since BpmnCopyPaste re-selects the first task on paste, this preview provider picks up that single-selection and launches direct editing. Any paste flag logic could prevent this activation.
2.bug_scenario: When copying and pasting a set of BPMN elements where the first element in the clipboard is a Task, that first pasted Task immediately enters “direct editing” mode (i.e. its label text field is focused and ready to edit). In the reproduced GIF the user selects three tasks, copies them, pastes them onto the canvas, and sees that the first of those three Tasks goes directly into inline label–edit mode. This should not happen on paste – direct editing should only be triggered for new shapes on manual creation, not on paste.
